h: Reading Divine Hints and Foreseeing the Need for Restraint

p: "Why was the parshah of the nazir placed
next to the parshah of the sotah?
that whoever sees a sotah in her disgrace
the parshah of the nazir is stated
after the parshah of the sotah,
while in the Oral Torah, in the Gemara,
because he sees another who went astray?
that it is like what our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
"He signals with a pointer before the king";
the way is to hint with hints.
before the King of the kings of kings;
and the hints are the heavenly voice
the thoughts of teshuvah in the heart,
that he should take from them
כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵהָרַבִּי רַבִּי זוּשָׁא זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
as is known of the Rebbe Reb Zusha, may the memory of the tzaddik be a blessing,
that he was walking on the road,
and it happened that there fell over
a gentile's wagon loaded with hay
to help him raise it up;
and he answered that he could not.
but you do not want to."
The Rebbe Reb Zusha said to himself:
hinting at the lower hei, which has fallen,
and I am able to raise it up,
and I do not want to.
that happen before a person's eyes
Therefore in the Written Torah is mentioned
for from the fact that it happened that he saw this,
And in the Oral Torah, in the Gemara,
And this is like what our Sages, of blessed memory, said
"One who foresees what will come about";
that is, by virtue of his wisdom
what could come about from it,
that this is what it says in the holy Zohar:
"The wise are greater than the prophets;
the holy spirit rests at times,
but upon the wise at every hour."
and it is only when it happens to him;
הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁרוֹאֶה תָּמִיד אֶת הַנּוֹלָד
that is, one who always foresees what will come about,
הוּא רוֹאֶה בְּכָל עֵת וּבְכָל שָׁעָה
he sees at every time and at every hour,
so that he knows to be careful
גַּם אִם לֹא נִזְדַּמֵּן עוֹד לְפָנָיו
even if it has not yet happened to him.
